# Proposal: Guided AI GRC Build for Tamarack Instruments (fictional)

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel
**Program:** Guided AI GRC Build, AI Governance Academy
**Duration and price:** 12 weeks, US$60,000

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It has about 1,100 staff and is headquartered in the Netherlands, with operations in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. Its AI portfolio is at three stages:

* **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
* **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
* **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

The regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. ISO/IEC 42001 work is planned to start next year, and that start date is not yet fixed. In June 2026 an internal audit finding recorded that there is no inventory of AI systems.

Dana Whitfield has stated the objective directly: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." The engagement must also respect three stated constraints:

* Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
* Customer data must stay in the EU.
* The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.

The Client already operates an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, an ISO 9001 quality management system and an internal audit function. This proposal treats those as structures to integrate with rather than duplicate. The specific registers, procedures and records within them that the AI management system should attach to are `Unknown` and will be confirmed at intake.

## 2. Why a Guided Build Rather Than Consulting Delivery

A conventional consulting engagement would deliver a set of governance documents to Tamarack Instruments. The Guided AI GRC Build works differently. The Client's own team builds the Artificial Intelligence Management System (AIMS) during the twelve weeks, with workshops, coaching and structured asynchronous work supporting each step.

At Week 12 the people who will run the system are the people who built it. They understand why each control exists and can operate, evidence and improve the system without depending on an outside party. This matters in three ways for Tamarack Instruments:

* **Audit continuity.** The internal audit finding on the AI inventory will be answered by a process the Client owns, not a document it received.
* **A head start on ISO/IEC 42001.** Planned ISO/IEC 42001 work will start from an operating base with evidence already accumulating.
* **Governance ahead of production.** Governance for the visual inspection pilot will be built by the roles that will carry it into production.

The program applies three principles throughout.

* **Slow AI:** AI that cannot be governed, explained and audited is not deployed; the three tests are conjunctive, and the doctrine is a precondition, not a speed limit.
* **Informed Intent:** no AI system acts without prior authorization stating its purpose, authority, boundaries and exit, given by a human who meets the five authorizer conditions.
* **Final Liability rests with the Human:** every material outcome attaches to a named human owner with decision rights, oversight and the power to intervene.

Delivery draws on two frameworks:

* GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
* Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)

Board-level reporting references AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

## 3. The Twelve-Week Spine, Tailored to Tamarack Instruments

**Inventory order.** The program proposes to enter systems into the inventory in this order:

1. **Customer service chatbot first.** It is the system already deployed and it faces customers.
2. **Visual inspection pilot second.** The stated Q2 2027 production objective makes it the governance priority.
3. **Sales forecasting third.** It enters as a planned system so that Informed Intent applies before it is built rather than after.

**ISO/IEC 42001 mapping.** The ISO/IEC 42001 column below shows readiness themes only. It is not a statement of conformity or a promise of certification.

**Integration points.** An integration point is named only where the artifact it attaches to is known. All others are `Unknown`.

| Week | Focus | Tailoring for Tamarack Instruments | ISO/IEC 42001 readiness theme | Integration point |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | Mobilization, charter and roles | Draft AIMS charter. Assign named owners under Final Liability rests with the Human. Confirm steering membership. | Context, leadership, roles | `Unknown` |
| W2 | AI system inventory | Inventory the chatbot, the visual inspection pilot and planned sales forecasting, in that order. Set up the process to keep the inventory current. | Context, operational planning | Responds to the June 2026 internal audit finding of no AI inventory |
| W3 | Classification and risk methodology | Classify each system against EU AI Act and GDPR considerations (confirm with external counsel). Agree a risk methodology. | Planning, risk criteria | `Unknown` |
| W4 | Risk and impact assessments | Assess the chatbot and the visual inspection pilot. Plan works council consultation for any production staff impact (confirm with external counsel). | AI risk and impact assessment | `Unknown` |
| W5 | Risk register and treatment | Build an operating register with treatment owners. | Risk treatment | `Unknown` |
| W6 | Policy set and mid-point steering | Draft and adopt the core AI policy set, then hold the mid-point steering checkpoint. | AI policy, leadership | `Unknown` |
| W7 | Operating procedures and lifecycle governance | Write lifecycle procedures covering design to retirement, including the pilot-to-production gate for visual inspection. | Operation, lifecycle | `Unknown` |
| W8 | Vendor and supplier governance; evidence collection begins | Supplier review, including EU customer data residency requirements (confirm with external counsel). Evidence collection starts. | Supplier relationships, documented information | `Unknown` |
| W9 | Governed workflows and human oversight | Configure at least two governed AI workflows using Slow AI Kitchen, with human oversight points. | Operation, human oversight | `Unknown` |
| W10 | Testing, evaluation and monitoring | Set evaluation criteria and monitoring for each governed workflow. | Performance evaluation | `Unknown` |
| W11 | Incident response, change management and evidence review | Define AI incident and change processes. Review the first weeks of evidence. | Improvement, nonconformity | `Unknown` |
| W12 | Audit readiness review, evidence walkthrough and closing steering | Walk through the evidence and attest against the minimum viable AIMS definition at closing steering. | Internal audit readiness, management review | `Unknown` |

**Questions to confirm at intake:**

* Which existing ISMS and QMS artifacts (for example risk registers, document control, supplier assessment, corrective action records) the AIMS should attach to.
* Whether the chatbot processes customer data and where that data is held.
* Whether the visual inspection workflow touches production staff.
* Which two workflows will be in production use by Week 12. The deployed chatbot is a candidate. Whether the visual inspection pilot can be the second depends on its production timing and works council consultation, both of which are `Unknown`.

## 4. Contracted Outcome: Minimum Viable AIMS at Week 12

The contracted outcome is a functioning minimum viable AIMS, defined as:

1. An adopted charter.
2. A populated inventory.
3. An operating risk register.
4. An adopted core policy set.
5. At least two governed AI workflows in production use.
6. Evidence collection running for at least four weeks.

This outcome positions Tamarack Instruments for its planned ISO/IEC 42001 work. It does not constitute certification, an audit opinion or a determination of regulatory compliance. Any item with legal effect, including EU AI Act classification, GDPR assessments and works council consultation, carries the note: confirm with external counsel.

## 5. Client Team Commitment

All figures below are **estimates** and include the weekly workshop, the coaching session and asynchronous work. Actual effort will vary by week. For example, the German plant manager's load is expected to rise in Weeks 4, 7 and 9, and the Head of Data's in Weeks 2, 8 and 10.

| Role | Estimated hours per week | Primary contribution |
|---|---|---|
| General Counsel | 3 to 4 (estimate) | Charter, policy set, legal review routing |
| CISO | 3 to 5 (estimate) | ISMS integration, supplier and data residency controls, incident response |
| Head of Quality | 3 to 5 (estimate) | QMS integration, procedures, change management |
| Head of Data | 4 to 6 (estimate) | Inventory, classification, evaluation and monitoring |
| German plant manager | 2 to 4 (estimate) | Visual inspection assessment, oversight design, works council coordination |
| Internal auditors (two) | 1 to 3 each (estimate) | Assurance perspective, evidence design, Week 12 readiness review |

**Internal audit independence.** The program proposes that the two internal auditors participate in an advisory and assurance capacity rather than as control owners. This preserves their independence for future audit of the AIMS. The Client should confirm this arrangement at intake.

**Workflow owners.** A named owner for each governed workflow is required under Final Liability rests with the Human. Those owners are `Unknown` and will be confirmed at Week 1.

## 6. Steering Cadence

Executive steering checkpoints occur at three points:

* **Week 1:** mobilization brief, scope and decisions needed.
* **Week 6:** mid-point report, blockers and scope decisions.
* **Week 12:** closing report and attestation against the minimum viable AIMS definition.

Steering membership is `Unknown` and will be confirmed at intake. Where board reporting is required, the closing report can draw on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

## 7. Logistics and Price

* **Format:** one live virtual workshop, one coaching session and structured asynchronous implementation each week, over 12 weeks.
* **Session scheduling:** session times across the Client's operating jurisdictions will be set at intake.
* **Start date:** `Unknown`.
* **Price:** US$60,000. This sits within the stated approved budget of up to US$80,000 for this fiscal year. Whether the engagement dates fall within that fiscal year is a question to confirm at intake.

## 8. Next Step

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. The proposed next step is an intake session to confirm:

* Start date.
* Build team availability.
* Steering membership.
* Candidate governed workflows.
* Integration points with the ISMS and QMS.
* The questions listed in Section 3.

On confirmation, Week 1 mobilization materials will be issued to the build team.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.
